docs.title: Harbor MCP server
docs.text:
A Model Context Protocol server for Harbor, the open-source container registry. It lets AI assistants such as Claude, Cursor and VS Code answer questions about a running Harbor: projects and quotas, repositories and artifacts, vulnerability scan results, robot accounts, replication health and garbage collection.

Ask things like:

  • Which artifacts in payments have critical vulnerabilities, and when were they last pulled?
  • Which robot accounts expire in the next 30 days, and what can they push?
  • Is replication to the edge registry healthy? When did it last succeed?
  • Which projects are close to their storage quota?
  • Install: container image, binaries or go install.
  • Connect a client: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code.
  • Read-only identity: a Harbor robot account that can only read.
  • Tools: the tools and their arguments.

docs.title: Design in short
docs.text:
• Read-only. Twelve tools cover projects, repositories, artifacts, vulnerabilities, robots, members, registries, replication, webhooks and garbage collection. No tool changes or deletes anything.
  • Secrets stay out of the conversation. Harbor credentials, robot secrets and webhook authorization headers never appear in tool results, logs or errors; a test enforces it.
  • Two transports. stdio for desktop clients, and streamable HTTP with a bearer token for running in a cluster (HTTP mode).
  • Signed and listed. A signed multi-arch image, ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp, listed in the official MCP Registry as io.github.oreondev/harbor-mcp.
  • Tested against real Harbor. Harbor 2.15 on every pull request and 2.12 to 2.15 nightly, as an administrator and as the read-only robot.

It uses the Harbor client of the Harbor Resource Operator, the Kubernetes operator that manages Harbor projects, robot accounts and replication as code.

Note

This is an independent community project, maintained by Oreon IT. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Harbor project or the CNCF; Harbor is a trademark of The Linux Foundation.

docs.title: Harbor MCP server: design
docs.text: Status: version 0.1.0 is released with the read tools (section 4), both transports and the release workflow. Version 0.5, 2026-11-04.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI assistants (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Docker's MCP Toolkit, ToolHive on Kubernetes) answer questions about a running Harbor: which projects exist and how full their quotas are, what was pushed recently, which artifacts have critical vulnerabilities, whether replication is healthy, which robot accounts expire soon. It reuses the Harbor client and the fake Harbor from harbor-resource-operator (pkg/harbor, pkg/harbor/fake), which are tested against Harbor 2.12 to 2.15, pinned to an operator release.

Scope matches the operator's: objects inside a running Harbor through API v2.0. It does not install Harbor, does not move image contents (the one exception is reading agent skills, section 10, which are small text artifacts), and never deletes anything.

On 2026-11-03 no maintained Harbor MCP server existed: bupd/harbor-mcp-server (TypeScript, 12 tools, last push 2026-02-20, not official), nomagicln/mcp-harbor (archived), and no Harbor entry in the official MCP Registry.

docs.title: 2. Shape
docs.text: Item Choice Binary cmd/harbor-mcp in this repository, module github.com/oreondev/harbor-mcp, released from its own vX.Y.Z tags Image ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp:X.Y.Z, multi-arch (amd64, arm64), distroless, non-root, signed with cosign, SBOM and provenance SDK github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk (official Go SDK, v1.8.0 on 2026-11-03) Transports stdio (default; for desktop clients and Docker's toolkit) and streamable HTTP with -http <addr> (for ToolHive, kmcp or a Deployment): MCP at /mcp, an unauthenticated GET /healthz for probes, stateless sessions so replicas need no affinity, cross-origin browser requests refused. TLS is left to the ingress or mesh in front Registry name io.github.oreondev/harbor-mcp (namespace proved by GitHub Actions OIDC in the release workflow) Licence Apache-2.0, same as the repository

docs.title: 3. Configuration
docs.text:
Environment variables, each with a _FILE variant for mounted Secrets:

Variable Meaning HARBOR_URL Harbor base URL, https://harbor.example.com HARBOR_USERNAME, HARBOR_PASSWORD Credentials. The documented setup is a system robot account with read permissions only; admin works but is not recommended HARBOR_CA_FILE Extra CA bundle (PEM) HARBOR_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY true to skip TLS verification; logged as a warning at start HARBOR_MCP_RATE Requests per second to Harbor, default 10, shared by all tools (the operator's limiter) HARBOR_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE true registers the write tools (section 5); off by default HARBOR_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN Bearer token required on every HTTP request in -http mode; the server refuses to start in HTTP mode without one unless -http binds to a loopback address HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_DIR Absolute path; registers harbor_install_skill (section 10.3) HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_REQUIRE_SIGNED false lets harbor_install_skill install unsigned skills; default true

Credentials and the HTTP token are never logged, never returned in tool output and never included in error messages. Robot secrets and webhook auth_header values are removed from every result.

docs.title: 4. Read tools (first release)
docs.text:
Every read tool carries the MCP annotations readOnlyHint: true and openWorldHint: true. Lists take query (name filter), page and pageSize (default 25, maximum 100) and report the total, so an assistant can page instead of receiving thousands of rows. Results are JSON (structuredContent with an output schema, also sent as text). Times are RFC 3339 strings in UTC, empty when Harbor has none (an artifact never pulled).

Tool Harbor endpoints Returns harbor_system_info GET /systeminfo, GET /users/current version, auth mode, the identity the server runs as harbor_list_projects GET /projects name, ID, public, repository count, auto-scan, proxy cache, created (quota is in harbor_get_project, to keep a page at one request) harbor_get_project GET /projects/{name}, GET /quotas?reference=project&reference_id=, GET /projects/{id}/immutabletagrules metadata, quota, CVE allowlist, whether a retention policy is set, number of immutable rules harbor_list_repositories GET /projects/{name}/repositories name, artifact count, pull count, last update harbor_list_artifacts GET /projects/{name}/repositories/{repo}/artifacts?with_tag=true&with_scan_overview=true digest, tags, size, push and pull time, scan status and severity counts harbor_get_vulnerabilities GET .../artifacts/{reference}/additions/vulnerabilities the scan report for one artifact, most severe first, filtered by minSeverity (default High) and capped by limit (at most 100), with counts by severity; a project without a scanner (Harbor's 404 "no scanner registration") is a note, not an error harbor_list_robots GET /robots name, level, permissions, disabled, expiry and whether expired (secrets never); optional filters by project and name harbor_list_members GET /projects/{name}/members entity, type, role harbor_list_registries GET /registries name, type, URL, health status (credentials never) harbor_list_replications GET /replication/policies, GET /replication/executions?policy_id= policy, direction, trigger, enabled, last execution status and counts harbor_list_webhooks GET /projects/{name}/webhook/policies name, events, targets (address and type; auth_header removed) harbor_get_gc GET /system/gc/schedule, GET /system/gc schedule and the last run

The client gains list methods for projects, repositories, artifacts and vulnerability reports (added in the operator repository, then pinned here); the rest exist already. The fake server (pkg/harbor/fake) gets the same endpoints, with the documented quirks kept (job_parameters as a JSON string, empty 200 body for no GC schedule).

docs.title: 5. Write tools (opt-in)
docs.text:
Registered only with HARBOR_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE=true, annotated readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: false, idempotentHint where true. None of them deletes or overwrites data.

Tool Harbor endpoint harbor_scan_artifact POST .../artifacts/{reference}/scan harbor_start_replication POST /replication/executions harbor_add_artifact_label POST .../artifacts/{reference}/labels harbor_create_project POST /projects (name, public, quota; nothing else)

Not offered in any mode: deleting projects, repositories, artifacts, tags or robots; creating robot accounts (the secret would land in a chat transcript; use the operator's HarborRobotAccount, which writes it to a Secret); user, LDAP, OIDC and system configuration changes.

docs.title: 6. Errors
docs.text: Harbor errors map to MCP tool errors (isError: true) with Harbor's status code and message, so the assistant can explain them: 401 and 403 name the missing permission, 404 says what was not found, 429 and 5xx say to retry. A 500 on a deleted retention policy is reported as "not found", as in the operator.

docs.title: 7. Testing
docs.text:
• Unit tests for every tool against the fake Harbor, through the SDK's in-memory transport, so the JSON schemas and annotations are tested as clients see them.
  • A test that no tool result contains the configured password, the HTTP token, a robot secret or a webhook auth_header.
  • An e2e test that starts the binary against a real Harbor from the official chart on kind and calls each read tool, on Harbor 2.12 to 2.15 like the operator.
  • make lint at 0 issues.

docs.title: 8. Packaging and listings
docs.text:
• Release workflow (a vX.Y.Z tag on main): build, push and sign ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp, with the label io.modelcontextprotocol.server.name=io.github.oreondev/harbor-mcp that the registry checks; then publish server.json to the official MCP Registry with mcp-publisher and GitHub OIDC. The registry feeds GitHub's MCP registry, VS Code and other clients.
  • server.json lives at the repository root and is versioned with the release.
  • After the first release, one submission each: Docker MCP Catalog (docker/mcp-registry), ToolHive catalog (stacklok/toolhive-catalog), LobeHub (lhm CLI), a Cursor marketplace plugin that wraps the server, Smithery and mcp.so. Each listing sets the homepage to the documentation page and states that the server is a community project, not affiliated with the Harbor project or the CNCF.
  • Helm: a small hand-written chart charts/harbor-mcp for HTTP mode (Deployment, Service, Secret reference, NetworkPolicy), from the second release on.

docs.title: 9. Order of work
docs.text:
1. Client list methods and fake endpoints, with tests, in the operator repository; pin that commit here.
  2. Server skeleton: configuration, stdio transport, harbor_system_info, the in-memory test harness.
  3. The other read tools.
  4. HTTP transport with the bearer token.
  5. Image, signing, server.json, registry publishing in the release workflow; README section.
  6. e2e spec.
  7. Listings (section 8).
  8. Write tools, then the Helm chart.

docs.title: 10. Agent skills
docs.text: Harbor as the registry for the agent skills a team writes: a skill (a folder with SKILL.md, as in the Agent Skills format) is pushed to a Harbor project as an OCI artifact, signed, and listed, read and installed through this server. Design version 2026-11-06.

docs.title: 10.1 Format
docs.text:
The Agent Skills OCI artifacts spec (v0.1.0 draft, April 2026). On 2026-11-06 it had the most implementations (arconia-cli, salaboy/skills-oci), NVIDIA's agent-package-spec builds on it, and it can be pushed with plain ORAS. One manifest per skill version:

Field Value artifactType application/vnd.agentskills.skill.v1 config application/vnd.agentskills.skill.config.v1+json (name, description and the other SKILL.md frontmatter) one layer application/vnd.agentskills.skill.content.v1.tar+gzip, rooted at <skill-name>/ annotations io.agentskills.skill.name (required), org.opencontainers.image.{title,description,version,source,revision,licenses} tags the version (1.2.0, immutable by a tag rule), plus latest

Convention: one repository per skill, <project>/<skill-name>. Other formats (NVIDIA, ToolHive, Alibaba ACR) are listed with their type but not read until one of them is adopted more widely.

docs.title: 10.2 What Harbor does with it (checked on Harbor 2.15, 2026-11-06)
docs.text:
• The artifact gets type: SKILL (Harbor's default processor derives it from the config media type), artifact_type, the manifest annotations, and the config JSON as extra_attrs. Listing skills needs only the REST API; q=type=SKILL filters a repository's artifacts.
  • GET /v2/<project>/<repo>/manifests/<ref> and /blobs/<digest> accept basic auth, so reading a skill needs no token service.
  • With the project's enable_content_trust_cosign on, a manifest pull of an unsigned artifact returns 412 PROJECTPOLICYVIOLATION "The image is not signed by cosign."; a blob pull by digest is not checked. This server therefore always resolves the manifest first, so the project policy decides whether a skill can be read.
  • Harbor's scanners only take IMAGE artifacts (controller/scan/util.go, read in the source), so Harbor does not scan skills. Scanning happens in CI before the push (NVIDIA SkillSpector or Cisco skill-scanner, both Apache-2.0); the report can be attached as a referrer (an attestation) next to the signature.

docs.title: 10.3 Tools
docs.text:
Read tools, registered by default (they read only what the robot can pull):

Tool Harbor calls Returns harbor_list_skills GET /projects/{p}/repositories, then GET .../artifacts?q=type=SKILL&with_tag=true&with_accessory=true per repository per skill: name, description, version, tags, digest, push time, whether a cosign signature is attached; paged over repositories harbor_get_skill the artifact, then GET /v2/.../manifests/{ref} and /blobs/{layer} the SKILL.md text, the file list with sizes, digest, version, signed; optional path returns one other text file of the skill

Install, registered only when HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_DIR is set (stdio use; in HTTP mode the directory would be on the server, which is rarely what the user wants, so the server warns):

Tool Does harbor_install_skill reads the skill as harbor_get_skill does, writes it to a temporary directory inside <dir> through os.Root, with .harbor-skill.json (repository, digest, version, signed), and renames it to <dir>/<skill-name>/. Refuses when that path exists and is not a directory with a marker naming the same repository (a symlink, a file, a directory it did not install); a failed install leaves the old one in place. A skill that carries its own marker file is refused. With HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_REQUIRE_SIGNED=true (default) it refuses a skill without a cosign signature accessory. Annotated destructive and idempotent; one install at a time

Permissions: listing needs only what the documented robot has. Reading and installing need repository:pull, which that robot does not have; the docs add a second project-level entry granting repository:pull on the skills projects only (namespace: "skills", not *), so the robot still cannot read image contents elsewhere. Without it the tools report Harbor's 401 or 403 with that hint.

Limits on every read: compressed layer at most 1 MiB, unpacked at most 4 MiB and 500 entries; only regular files and directories; no absolute paths, .., symlinks or hard links; mode bits limited to 0644 and 0755. Text returned to the model is capped at 64 KiB per file. A skill is instructions for the model, so tool results say which project and digest it came from and whether it is signed.

Signing: the server checks that a signature exists; it does not verify it cryptographically. Verification is Harbor's job (enableContentTrustCosign on the project, which Harbor enforces at pull time; keyless identities are checked by cosign verify in CI). The docs recommend the policy for every skills project.

docs.title: 10.4 Client and fake (operator repository first)
docs.text:
• Artifact gains ArtifactType, Annotations, ExtraAttrs and Accessories (type, digest); ListArtifactsOfType(ctx, project, repo, type, po) adds q=type=<T> and with_accessory=true.
  • GetManifest(ctx, project, repo, ref) and GetBlob(ctx, project, repo, digest, limit) on the registry API (/v2/, basic auth, digest checked, limit enforced while reading). A 412 policy violation becomes an APIError with Harbor's message.
  • The fake stores manifests, blobs, artifact types and accessories, filters by q=type=, and can enforce the cosign policy per project, with the 412 body above.

docs.title: 10.5 Around the server
docs.text:
• Push: documented with ORAS (oras push --artifact-type application/vnd.agentskills.skill.v1 --config ...) and a GitHub Actions workflow: pack, scan with SkillSpector, push to Harbor, cosign sign keyless, attach the scan report. No CLI of our own; arconia-cli and skr exist.
  • Operator: a sample for a skills project: HarborProject with enableContentTrustCosign, an immutable tag rule for version tags, a retention policy keeping the last ten versions, a CI robot that can push and an agent robot that can only pull.
  • Docs: a "Skills in Harbor" page on both sites, and a blog post.

docs.title: 10.6 Order of work
docs.text:
1. Client and fake in the operator repository (10.4), with tests and a Harbor e2e check; release the operator patch and bump the pin here.
  2. harbor_list_skills and harbor_get_skill, with tests against the fake, including the unpack limits and a hostile tarball.
  3. harbor_install_skill.
  4. e2e on kind: push a skill with oras-go, sign it with cosign, list, read and install it as the read-only robot, with the project policy on and off.
  5. Operator sample, push workflow, docs page, blog post.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes are listed here, newest first. Versions follow semantic versioning. Each release also has a GitHub release with the image digest, binaries and signed checksums.

• Agent skills stored in Harbor as OCI artifacts (the Agent Skills OCI artifacts format): harbor_list_skills lists the skills in a project with version, tags and whether they are signed; harbor_get_skill returns a skill's SKILL.md or another of its files, read through the manifest so the project's cosign policy applies, with size, path and link checks on the content. Reading a skill needs repository:pull on its project (#20).
  • harbor_install_skill, registered only when HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_DIR is set, installs a skill into that directory with a .harbor-skill.json marker; it replaces only its own earlier install of the same repository and refuses unsigned skills unless HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_REQUIRE_SIGNED=false (#20).
  • An Agent skills docs page: pushing with ORAS, signing, the extra repository:pull permission for the skills project, and installing. The end-to-end suite pushes, signs, lists, reads and installs a skill as that robot, with the project's cosign policy off and on (#20).
  • Harbor error messages no longer end in a double full stop when the server adds a hint (#20).

• Documentation site at https://www.oreonit.com/harbor-mcp/, with a tool reference generated from the server, and these release notes (#10).
  • harbor-mcp -list-tools prints every tool with its schemas and annotations as JSON (#10).
  • Builds from go install report the module version instead of dev (#10).
  • The MCP Registry entry links to the documentation site (websiteUrl).

First release.

  • Twelve read-only tools: harbor_system_info, harbor_list_projects, harbor_get_project, harbor_list_repositories, harbor_list_artifacts, harbor_get_vulnerabilities, harbor_list_members, harbor_list_robots, harbor_list_registries, harbor_list_replications, harbor_list_webhooks and harbor_get_gc. None of them changes anything in Harbor.
  • stdio, and streamable HTTP with a bearer token.
  • A documented read-only robot account (docs/read-only-robot.json) that every tool works with.
  • Image ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp for amd64 and arm64, and binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows, all signed with cosign; listed in the MCP Registry as io.github.oreondev/harbor-mcp.
  • Tested end to end on kind against Harbor 2.15; the nightly run covers 2.12 to 2.15.

docs.title: Connect a client
docs.text:
Every client starts the server the same way: the container image (or the binary) with HARBOR_URL, HARBOR_USERNAME and HARBOR_PASSWORD. Use the read-only robot as the user.

Claude CodeClaude Desktop / CursorVS CodeBinary 
claude mcp add harbor -e HARBOR_URL=https://harbor.example.com -e 'HARBOR_USERNAME=robot$harbor-mcp' -e HARBOR_PASSWORD=... \
  -- docker run -i --rm -e HARBOR_URL -e HARBOR_USERNAME -e HARBOR_PASSWORD ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp:0.2.0

Or, for a shared HTTP server:

claude mcp add --transport http harbor https://harbor-mcp.example.com/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HARBOR_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN"

In claude_desktop_config.json, or Cursor's ~/.cursor/mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "harbor": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "-e", "HARBOR_URL", "-e", "HARBOR_USERNAME", "-e", "HARBOR_PASSWORD",
               "ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp:0.2.0"],
      "env": {
        "HARBOR_URL": "https://harbor.example.com",
        "HARBOR_USERNAME": "robot$harbor-mcp",
        "HARBOR_PASSWORD": "..."
      }
    }
  }
}

In .vscode/mcp.json; VS Code asks for the password once and stores it:

{
  "inputs": [
    { "type": "promptString", "id": "harbor-password", "description": "Harbor robot secret", "password": true }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "harbor": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "docker",
      "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "-e", "HARBOR_URL", "-e", "HARBOR_USERNAME", "-e", "HARBOR_PASSWORD",
               "ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp:0.2.0"],
      "env": {
        "HARBOR_URL": "https://harbor.example.com",
        "HARBOR_USERNAME": "robot$harbor-mcp",
        "HARBOR_PASSWORD": "${input:harbor-password}"
      }
    }
  }
}

Without Docker, use the binary as the command and pass the same variables in env:

{ "command": "harbor-mcp", "env": { "HARBOR_URL": "https://harbor.example.com", "HARBOR_USERNAME": "robot$harbor-mcp", "HARBOR_PASSWORD": "..." } }

Then ask, for example, "What Harbor version is this, and who am I connected as?": the assistant calls harbor_system_info and should answer with the version and robot$harbor-mcp.

Harbor with a private CA

Mount the CA into the container and set HARBOR_CA_FILE, for example -v /etc/ssl/harbor-ca.pem:/ca.pem:ro -e HARBOR_CA_FILE=/ca.pem.

docs.title: HTTP mode
docs.text:
For a shared server, for example a Deployment next to Harbor, start it with -http and a token:

docker run -d -p 8080:8080 \
  -e HARBOR_URL -e HARBOR_USERNAME -e HARBOR_PASSWORD -e HARBOR_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN \
  ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp:0.2.0 -http :8080
  • MCP is served at /mcp (streamable HTTP, stateless: any replica can serve any request).
  • Every request needs Authorization: Bearer <HARBOR_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN>; others get 401.
  • GET /healthz is open, for liveness and readiness probes.
  • Browser cross-origin requests are refused.
  • Without a token the server refuses to listen beyond a loopback address.
  • TLS is left to what is in front of it: an ingress, a gateway or a service mesh.

Clients connect with the URL and the header:

claude mcp add --transport http harbor https://harbor-mcp.example.com/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HARBOR_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN"

docs.title: On Kubernetes
docs.text:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: harbor-mcp
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: harbor-mcp } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: harbor-mcp } }
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: harbor-mcp
        image: ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp:0.2.0
        args: ["-http", ":8080"]
        env:
        - { name: HARBOR_URL, value: https://harbor.example.com }
        - { name: HARBOR_USERNAME_FILE, value: /secrets/username }
        - { name: HARBOR_PASSWORD_FILE, value: /secrets/password }
        - { name: HARBOR_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN_FILE, value: /secrets/token }
        ports: [{ containerPort: 8080 }]
        readinessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 8080 } }
        livenessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 8080 } }
        volumeMounts: [{ name: secrets, mountPath: /secrets, readOnly: true }]
      volumes:
      - name: secrets
        secret: { secretName: harbor-mcp }   # keys: username, password, token

Put a Service and your usual ingress with TLS in front of it.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Container imageBinarygo install 
docker pull ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp:0.2.0

Multi-arch (amd64, arm64), distroless, non-root, about 12 MB. Verify the signature:

cosign verify ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp:0.2.0 \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/oreondev/harbor-mcp/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com

Download the archive for your platform (Linux, macOS, Windows; amd64 and arm64) from the releases. checksums.txt is signed; verify it with:

cosign verify-blob --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/oreondev/harbor-mcp/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com checksums.txt
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt

go install github.com/oreondev/harbor-mcp/cmd/harbor-mcp@v0.2.0

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configuration comes from environment variables. Each one except HARBOR_CA_FILE can instead be read from a file named by <NAME>_FILE, for mounted secrets.

Variable Meaning HARBOR_URL Harbor base URL, for example https://harbor.example.com (required) HARBOR_USERNAME, HARBOR_PASSWORD The account the server acts as; use the read-only robot (required) HARBOR_CA_FILE Extra CA bundle (PEM) for Harbor's certificate HARBOR_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY true to skip TLS verification of Harbor HARBOR_MCP_RATE Requests per second to Harbor, default 10 HARBOR_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN Bearer token for HTTP mode HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_DIR Absolute path of a skills directory (for example /home/me/.claude/skills); registers harbor_install_skill, which installs skills from Harbor there. Meant for stdio; in HTTP mode the skills land on the server's machine, and the server warns HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_REQUIRE_SIGNED false to let harbor_install_skill install skills without a cosign signature; default true

With Docker, mount the skills directory and run as your own user, so the installed files belong to you:

docker run -i --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$HOME/.claude/skills:/skills" -e HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_DIR=/skills \
  -e HARBOR_URL -e HARBOR_USERNAME -e HARBOR_PASSWORD ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-mcp:0.2.0

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Meaning -http <addr> Serve streamable HTTP on this address instead of stdio -list-tools Print the tool definitions as JSON and exit; needs no Harbor -version Print the version and exit

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Connect your AI client.

docs.title: Read-only identity
docs.text:
Run the server as a Harbor system robot account that can only read. read-only-robot.json is the request body for Harbor's API, with exactly the permissions the tools need. The end-to-end tests create the same robot and run every tool as it.

curl -u admin -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d @read-only-robot.json https://harbor.example.com/api/v2.0/robots

Harbor shows the secret once, in the response; the user name is robot$harbor-mcp. Store the secret in your client's configuration or a secret manager, not in a shared file.

docs.title: What it can read
docs.text:
Level Resources System projects, quotas, robot accounts, registries, replication policies and executions, garbage collection Every project project and metadata, quota, repositories, artifacts, tags, labels, artifact additions, scan reports, members, robot accounts, immutable tag rules, tag retention, webhook policies

Nothing in the list allows a change: no create, update, delete, push or pull.

Reading agent skills needs pull on the skills project; that page shows how to add it for that project only.

Note

The robot has no expiry (duration: -1). Set a duration in days if your policy requires rotation, and update the client's secret when you refresh it.

An administrator account also works, but gives the assistant far more than it needs.

docs.title: Agent skills in Harbor
docs.text:
An agent skill is a folder with a SKILL.md and, optionally, scripts and reference files. Harbor can store skills like images: one OCI artifact per version, in the Agent Skills OCI artifacts format, with tags, immutability, retention, replication and cosign signatures. The server then lets the assistant:

  • list the skills in a project (harbor_list_skills), with version, tags and whether each is signed;
  • read one (harbor_get_skill): its SKILL.md, its file list, or another of its files;
  • install one into your skills directory (harbor_install_skill), when you turn that on.

Use one project for skills (skills below) and one repository per skill.

docs.title: Push a skill
docs.text:
Pack the folder so the archive is rooted at the skill's name, write the config from the SKILL.md front matter, and push with ORAS:

tar czf review.tar.gz review/          # review/SKILL.md, review/scripts/...
echo '{"name":"review","description":"Reviews pull requests."}' > config.json
oras push harbor.example.com/skills/review:1.0.0 \
  --artifact-type application/vnd.agentskills.skill.v1 \
  --config config.json:application/vnd.agentskills.skill.config.v1+json \
  --annotation io.agentskills.skill.name=review \
  --annotation org.opencontainers.image.version=1.0.0 \
  review.tar.gz:application/vnd.agentskills.skill.content.v1.tar+gzip

Harbor shows the artifact with type SKILL.

docs.title: Sign it, and make Harbor enforce signatures
docs.text:
cosign sign --yes harbor.example.com/skills/review@sha256:...

Then turn on the project's cosign policy (in the Harbor UI: project, Configuration, "Cosign": prevent unsigned artifacts from being pulled; with the Harbor Resource Operator: enableContentTrustCosign: true on the HarborProject). Harbor then refuses to serve an unsigned skill, and the server says so. The server itself only checks that a signature is attached; Harbor's policy, or cosign verify in CI, checks who signed it.

Harbor's vulnerability scanners only handle images, so scan skills in CI before the push.

docs.title: Let the robot read skills
docs.text:
The read-only robot can list skills but not read their content: that needs repository:pull. Grant it on the skills project only, so the robot still cannot pull images elsewhere:

jq '.permissions += [{"kind": "project", "namespace": "skills",
      "access": [{"resource": "repository", "action": "pull"}]}]' \
  read-only-robot.json > skills-robot.json
curl -u admin -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d @skills-robot.json https://harbor.example.com/api/v2.0/robots

The project must exist before you create the robot. The end-to-end tests create the same robot.

docs.title: Install skills
docs.text:
Set HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_DIR to the absolute path of your client's skills directory, for example /home/me/.claude/skills for Claude Code. That registers harbor_install_skill, which:

  • writes the skill to <dir>/<name>/ with a .harbor-skill.json file naming the repository, digest and version;
  • replaces only its own earlier install of the same repository, and refuses any other file or folder of that name;
  • refuses skills without a cosign signature, unless HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_REQUIRE_SIGNED=false.

A skill is instructions your assistant will follow, written by whoever pushed it. Read it with harbor_get_skill before installing it; the tool's description asks the assistant to show it to you and ask first.

Install is meant for stdio, where the server runs on your machine. In HTTP mode the skills would land on the server's machine, and the server logs a warning. With Docker, mount the directory; see Install.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
The server has 15 tools, all read-only (readOnlyHint); none of them changes or deletes anything in Harbor. Lists are paged: page starts at 1, pageSize defaults to 25 and is at most 100. This page is generated from harbor-mcp -list-tools.

Tool What it answers harbor_get_gc Get garbage collection harbor_get_project Get a project harbor_get_skill Get a skill harbor_get_vulnerabilities Get vulnerabilities harbor_install_skill Install a skill harbor_list_artifacts List artifacts harbor_list_members List project members harbor_list_projects List projects harbor_list_registries List registries harbor_list_replications List replication policies harbor_list_repositories List repositories harbor_list_robots List robot accounts harbor_list_skills List skills harbor_list_webhooks List webhooks harbor_system_info Harbor system information

docs.title: harbor_get_gc
docs.text:
The garbage collection schedule and the outcome of the last garbage collection run.

No arguments.

Returns: cron, lastRun, nextRun, schedule, scheduled.

docs.title: harbor_get_project
docs.text:
One project in detail: visibility, storage quota and usage, vulnerability and signing policies, CVE allowlist, and whether retention and immutability rules are set.

Argument Type Required Description project string yes project name

Returns: autoScan, contentTrust, created, cveAllowlist, id, immutableRules, name, owner, preventVulnerable, proxyCache, public, quota, repositoryCount, retentionPolicy, severity, updated.

docs.title: harbor_get_skill
docs.text:
Read one agent skill from Harbor: its SKILL.md, the list of its files, digest, version and whether it is signed. Pass path to read one other text file of the skill. Needs pull permission on the project.

Argument Type Required Description path string a file of the skill to return instead of SKILL.md, as listed in files project string yes project name reference string tag or digest (sha256:...); default the newest version repository string yes the skill's repository, with or without the project prefix

Returns: content, digest, files, name, notice, path, signed, source, truncated, version.

docs.title: harbor_get_vulnerabilities
docs.text:
The vulnerabilities found in one artifact (by tag or digest), most severe first, at or above minSeverity (default High).

Argument Type Required Description limit integer most entries to return (default and maximum 100) minSeverity string Critical, High (default), Medium, Low, Negligible or Unknown project string yes project name reference string yes tag or digest (sha256:...) repository string yes repository name, with or without the project prefix

Returns: bySeverity, generated, matching, note, scanned, scanner, severity, vulnerabilities.

docs.title: harbor_install_skill
docs.text:
Install an agent skill from Harbor into the skills directory on this machine (HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_DIR), as //. Replaces an earlier install of the same repository; refuses a directory it did not install. Refuses unsigned skills unless HARBOR_MCP_SKILLS_REQUIRE_SIGNED=false. Show the user the skill (harbor_get_skill) and ask before installing it. Argument Type Required Description project string yes project name reference string tag or digest (sha256:...); default the newest version repository string yes the skill's repository, with or without the project prefix

Returns: digest, files, name, notice, path, replaced, signed, source, version.

docs.title: harbor_list_artifacts
docs.text:
List the artifacts (images, charts) of a repository, newest push first, with tags, size, labels and the result of the last vulnerability scan.

Argument Type Required Description page integer page number, starting at 1 (default 1) pageSize integer items per page (default 25, at most 100) project string yes project name repository string yes repository name, with or without the project prefix

Returns: items, page, pageSize, total.

docs.title: harbor_list_members
docs.text:
List the users and groups that are members of a project, with their roles.

Argument Type Required Description page integer page number, starting at 1 (default 1) pageSize integer items per page (default 25, at most 100) project string yes project name

Returns: items, page, pageSize, total.

docs.title: harbor_list_projects
docs.text:
List Harbor projects the server's user can see, optionally only those whose name contains query.

Argument Type Required Description page integer page number, starting at 1 (default 1) pageSize integer items per page (default 25, at most 100) query string only projects whose name contains this

Returns: items, page, pageSize, total.

docs.title: harbor_list_registries
docs.text:
List the remote registries (endpoints) Harbor replicates to or from, with their health. Credentials are never shown.

Argument Type Required Description page integer page number, starting at 1 (default 1) pageSize integer items per page (default 25, at most 100) query string only items whose name contains this

Returns: items, page, pageSize, total.

docs.title: harbor_list_replications
docs.text:
List replication policies with source, destination, trigger and the outcome of the last run.

Argument Type Required Description page integer page number, starting at 1 (default 1) pageSize integer items per page (default 25, at most 100) query string only items whose name contains this

Returns: items, page, pageSize, total.

docs.title: harbor_list_repositories
docs.text:
List the repositories of a project, optionally only those whose name contains query.

Argument Type Required Description page integer page number, starting at 1 (default 1) pageSize integer items per page (default 25, at most 100) project string yes project name query string only repositories whose name contains this

Returns: items, page, pageSize, total.

docs.title: harbor_list_robots
docs.text:
List robot accounts with their permissions and expiry, optionally only those with access to project or whose name contains query. Harbor lists project robots per project, so without project this makes one Harbor request per project. Secrets are never shown.

Argument Type Required Description page integer page number, starting at 1 (default 1) pageSize integer items per page (default 25, at most 100) project string only robots with permissions in this project query string only robots whose name contains this

Returns: items, page, pageSize, total.

docs.title: harbor_list_skills
docs.text:
List the agent skills stored in a project (OCI artifacts of type SKILL, one repository per skill): name, description, newest version and tags, and whether it is signed with cosign. Pages over the project's repositories; repositories without a skill are left out.

Argument Type Required Description page integer page number, starting at 1 (default 1) pageSize integer items per page (default 25, at most 100) project string yes project name query string only repositories whose name contains this

Returns: items, page, pageSize, repositoriesTotal.

docs.title: harbor_list_webhooks
docs.text:
List the webhook policies of a project: events and target addresses. Authorization headers are never shown, only whether one is set.

Argument Type Required Description page integer page number, starting at 1 (default 1) pageSize integer items per page (default 25, at most 100) project string yes project name

Returns: items, page, pageSize, total.

docs.title: harbor_system_info
docs.text:
Harbor version, authentication mode and URLs, and the user or robot account the server acts as (with whether it is a Harbor administrator).

No arguments.

Returns: admin, authMode, externalURL, harborVersion, registryURL, robot, user.
